titleEn: You Can Cry. I Will Hold Your Hand!

pages.text: "Look, an ice mirror!" Kiki, the pointy-eared cat, lifted the whole sheet of ice from the water bucket. It clung to the fingertips in the cold. "I will show Nono and Gugu!"
Kiki carried it down the alley in both hands. A slippery step! It slipped away. Crash! The ice broke into pieces on the stone paving.
Tears rose, but Kiki held them back. "Only babies cry." Lips pressed shut. Holding back made the throat hurt and the chest feel tight.
Grandpa Badger leaned his broom against the wall and knelt in the snow. "You may cry if you want. Holding it in hurts more." Their faces were level.
"It was the shiniest one... All broken." Kiki barely got the words out. "You must feel so sad. Tears are nothing to be ashamed of." Tears fell down Kiki's cheeks.
"Kiki is crying!" Nono, the smallest, roundest sparrow, ran up. Gugu, the broad-chested pigeon, came and held a hand. "You can cry. I will hold your hand!" Nono held the other.
Kiki cried freely. After a good long cry, the tight chest felt open. "I feel a little better now." Kiki sniffled and looked up.
Grandpa dried Kiki's cheeks. Kiki touched the green bell. Jingle! Nono and Gugu still held both hands.
Now Kiki knew what to do when upset. "Do not hold it in! Have a good cry! Ask someone to hold your hand!" The three sat by the bucket, looking at new ice.
Grandpa hugged all three together. A good cry makes your heart feel lighter. Kiki wiped away the tear marks. "You can cry. I will hold your hand!"
